relevance_note: Case report of an index girl and her mother carrying a PSTPIP1 variant: "A previously reported pathogenic mutation in PSTPIP1, c.748G > A, p.Glu250Lys, was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Segregation analysis confirmed that the mother harbored the same mutation".
method_note: Written by hand into a small Python builder; no table transcribed by script. Two in-scope people: the index patient (label 'patient' under rule 5, since 'index patient' is a role word) and her mother ('mother of patient'). The paper calls the disease PAMI syndrome, not PAPA. The mother's variant row uses the index patient's printed variant plus the sentence 'the mother harbored the same mutation'; her inheritance is not reported (her parents are not described). The father is never mentioned. Zygosity left 'not reported': the only 'heterozygous' statement is a general one in the Introduction, and the Fig. 1 legend gives an 'autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance', not a zygosity. Fig. 1B legend 'evidencing anemia, neutropenia in both patients and thrombocytopenia in the index patient' is ambiguous for anemia in the mother, so the mother's anemia is left 'not reported'; neutropenia in both is recorded. Mother: 'remained asymptomatic throughout adulthood' / 'completely asymptomatic' sits beside 'recurrent fever and thrombocytopenia since early in life' (childhood history, not a contradiction about the same time). Age 4 years is the age at which she 'came to our attention'; recorded as last evaluation because no later age is printed and Fig. 2 covers a four-year follow-up (uncertain). Onset 'in her first month of life' given no ISO value (ordinal, not an age). Arthritis is recorded observed from 'amelioration of diarrhea, skin rash and arthritis' after steroids. 'Recurrent infections' marked observed from 'antibiotics to treat undefined systemic infections' over several hospitalizations (judgement call). Normal B cells and normal IgM recorded as excluded abnormal levels (D-27). Table 1 and 2 flow-cytometry percentages were not turned into features beyond the text statements. Paper inconsistencies: hemoglobin '6.6 mg/dL' against a reference range in g/dL; the Conclusions call the variant 'E205k' while elsewhere it is E250K / p.Glu250Lys; the gene is misspelled 'PSTIPIP1' in places. Vital status not stated explicitly for either person.
